page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a-nps1.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated virtual CPU cores. The instance features 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB RAM per dedicated core.

Hardware architecture does not include onboard local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs. Persistent disk operations rely entirely on external network-attached block storage volumes over the instance's 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated Elastic IP or private network gateway configuration for external internet connectivity.

The 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation provides high resource density for workloads constrained by memory capacity rather than raw compute cycles. While relying on remote storage increases dependency on network throughput for input and output operations, the memory capacity reduces swapping and facilitates large in-memory working sets. The instance is suited for enterprise databases, in-memory caches, big data processing engines, and large-scale enterprise analytics.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a-nps1.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features a 64-vCPU dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processor based on the x86_64 architecture operating at 2.55 GHz. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation well suited for memory-intensive environments. The configuration includes no discrete GPU hardware and contains no local storage, directing all primary disk input and output operations across network-attached volumes supported by a 16 Gbps baseline network interface. Network ingress and egress exclude complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external IP management for public connectivity. With its extensive RAM allocation and dedicated compute cores, ecs.r7a-nps1.16xlarge is primarily designed for large in-memory databases, distributed caching clusters, business intelligence engines, and memory-heavy enterprise backend services.
